title: Fightback: Consumer TV device report
description: One observation report for a single television or streaming device. Carried as newline-delimited JSON, one report per line. This schema is the normative contract and the technical annex to PRIVACY.md. Fields that could identify a household are absent by design rather than optional, so a conforming report cannot carry them. additionalProperties is false at every level to enforce that.

schema_version.description: Released schema version. Unknown values are rejected rather than guessed at.

report_id.description: Random UUID v4 generated per report, for idempotency only. Must not be derived from any device state. Dropped from the published dataset.

submitter_key.description: SHA-256 of a locally generated salt concatenated with an install identifier. The salt never leaves the contributor's device, so we can count distinct contributors without being able to identify one. Rotate monthly. Never published.

submitted_at.description: UTC, rounded to the hour. Sub-hour precision is rejected because second-resolution viewing timestamps are viewing habits, which is what the FTC fined Vizio over.

tier.description: Provenance label, assigned server-side and ignored if a client sets it. 'verified' means the report was signed by a key from a reproducible release build. That is a cost boundary and a label, not a security boundary, because the key is extractable from any build.

capture_method.description: How the observation was made. This bounds what can be concluded from it: a resolver log shows names only, a packet capture also shows addresses and server name indication.

resolver_kind.description: Which resolver produced the log. Never the resolver's address or hostname.

model_family.description: Normalised family, not the raw regional SKU. 'LG OLED C3' rather than 'OLED55C34LA', because a full SKU plus a country plus a firmware version is a very small cohort.

os_major.description: Major version only. Full build strings such as 03.30.55 are near-unique per region and batch, so they are rejected.

region.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, uppercase. Country only. Never city, postcode, coordinates, timezone, or anything derived from an IP address.

locale.description: BCP 47 language, and script where it matters. No region subtag, since that would duplicate and sometimes contradict the region field.

app_inventory.description: Installed package or channel names. Defaults to null and requires a separate explicit opt-in, because an app list is a strong behavioural fingerprint. Names only, never versions.

acr_state.description: Whether content recognition was opted out when the observation was made. The central question this dataset answers, since the IMC 2024 study found opt-out stops the traffic and we want that verified independently per model and firmware.

account_signed_in.description: Boolean only. Never an account name, address, identifier, or hash of one.

fqdn_template.description: The publishable key. Lowercased, trailing dot stripped, internationalised names normalised, truncated to at most two labels above the registrable domain, with high-entropy labels replaced by {id} and numeric shard suffixes by {n}. A raw fully qualified name must never appear. The pattern permits only lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, dots, asterisks and the two placeholder tokens.

registrable_domain.description: Effective top-level domain plus one, resolved through the Public Suffix List. Always safe to publish.

original_label_count.description: Label depth before truncation. Preserves the analytic signal without the labels themselves.

redacted_label_count.description: How many labels were replaced. A non-zero value combined with a low contributor count means hard quarantine.

ja4.description: JA4 TLS client fingerprint only, which is BSD-3-Clause. The rest of the JA4+ family is patent-pending under a licence with commercial restrictions and is not collected. JA3 was archived in May 2025 and deprecated by its author.

bytes_up_bucket.description: Bucketed to a power of two, not exact. Exact byte counts over time are a viewing-behaviour side channel.

scenario.description: What the device was doing. Taxonomy adopted from the IMC 2024 study so results compare across research.

category.description: Assigned server-side only. A client-asserted category is ignored, because categorisation drives the blocklist tiers.

notes.description: Free text is a leak vector, so it is short, scrubbed for addresses and identifiers, and reviewed before any publication.

$comment: Fields deliberately absent so that a conforming report cannot carry them: src_ip, dest_ip, mac, oui, serial, device_id, ad_id, tifa, idfa, rida, ssid, bssid, client_hostname, client_name, lan_peer, url_path, query_string, http_headers, cookies, payload, body, tls_keylog, sslkeylogfile, lat, lon, city, postcode, timezone, account_id, account_email, exact_timestamp, dns_answer. additionalProperties is false at every object level, so any of these is a validation failure rather than an ignored extra key. See PRIVACY.md.
